The rhythmic whir of the ceiling fan did little to soothe my frayed nerves as I triple-checked our snorkeling gear by the hotel window. My sundress strap slid down my shoulder, but I made no move to fix it, too preoccupied with ensuring Sangwook and I were prepared for this afternoon's yacht trip to the reefs.

Five years had passed since our shy introduction in the university library stacks. Five years of subtle smiles across classrooms, stolen kisses between study sessions, the soft embrace of his jacket around my shoulders whenever evening chill crept through the city streets. Now here we sat, graduated and married, yet my heart still fluttered like a caged bird at his nearness.

Sangwook leaned against the headboard, bare chested and grinning, brandishing that tattered pamphlet like a winning lottery ticket. The words "Naturalist Cove" shouted up at me, brazen as the swath of skin peeking above his waistband. "Just *look* at the brochure before you decide," he insisted, eyes sparkling with mischief. "When else are we going to get this chance?"

I tucked a strand of hair behind my ear, fighting the embarrassed flush creeping into my cheeks as I imagined baring myself to a beach full of equally unclothed strangers. "I told you," I murmured, folding and refolding the same towel to busy my trembling hands, "seeing people's… *parts* baking in the sun isn't necessary for me to enjoy our honeymoon."

Sangwook threw himself back onto the mattress with a dramatic sigh, limbs sprawled in a careless X across the floral bedspread. "It’s about freedom, Eun-ei! About adventure!" His arm swept an expansive arc toward the balcony where heatwaves shimmered temptingly above the white sand shores, a dare lurking beneath his playfulness. "We’re twenty-six, not dead. What's life without a little spontaneity?"
